title: Custom Endpoint Descriptor
description: Defines a custom HTTP endpoint that executes server-side JavaScript code.
markdownDescription: AI guidance: use custom endpoints for model-owned actions and lightweight APIs. `name` must be unique within its app. `route` should start with `/api/` and must not conflict with another route/method. Use `{id}` style path parameters when needed. With `routeScope: "app"` the route is published beneath `/api/low-code/apps/<app>/endpoints` instead of verbatim. Scripts can access request data through the endpoint context and return HTTP results with helpers such as `context.ok(value)`, `context.created(value)`, and `context.noContent()` where available. Require authentication by default. Authorization is resolved in order: `requiredPermissions` when non-empty, otherwise `useResourceAuthorization: true` (per-endpoint resource permission), otherwise `requireAuthentication`.

$schema.description: Optional schema reference used when this descriptor is stored as a model descriptor file.

name.description: Unique endpoint identifier used by designer/model health. Prefer PascalCase or kebab-case, for example 'SearchCustomers'.

app.description: Name of the low-code app that owns this endpoint. Omit for the default app. Must match an apps[].name.

route.description: URL route pattern. Must start with '/' and should use an application-specific prefix such as '/api/low-code/events/{id}'. Route parameters use ASP.NET style braces, for example '{id}'. With routeScope 'app', this is appended to the app endpoint prefix.

routeScope.description: 'global' publishes route unchanged. 'app' publishes it beneath '/api/low-code/apps/<app>/endpoints'. Does not change ownership, authentication, or permissions.

method.description: HTTP method. GET should be read-only; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE may mutate state. Values are normalized to upper-case.

javascript.description: JavaScript code to execute. Use context request/response helpers and services exposed by the host, such as db, currentUser/currentTenant, authorization, emailSender, config, http, event bus, background jobs, and logging helpers.

requireAuthentication.description: Whether authentication is required. Keep true unless this endpoint is intentionally public.

useResourceAuthorization.description: When true and requiredPermissions is empty, access is granted per endpoint name through the generated ABP resource permission for this endpoint (with the global Low-Code endpoint permission as fallback). When requiredPermissions contains values, those permissions are checked instead.

requiredPermissions.description: Permission names required to access the endpoint. Permission checks imply authorization even when requireAuthentication is false. Values should reference custom permissions or known static permissions.

description.description: Optional human-readable description for designer documentation and model health context.

extendsLowerLayer.description: When true, this descriptor overrides selected fields of an endpoint with the same name defined in a lower model layer; route and javascript become optional.

examples.name: SearchCustomers
examples.javascript: var q = context.request.query.q || ''; var table = await db.query('Acme.Crm.Customer'); var rows = await table.where(c => c.Name.toLowerCase().includes(q.toLowerCase())).take(10).toList(); return context.ok(rows);
